candidate_concepts.label: Purpose of UML Deployment Diagrams
candidate_concepts.description: Deployment diagrams model the physical architecture of a system, showing the relationships between software and hardware components and the physical distribution of processing.
coverage_criteria: Student can state that deployment diagrams show the hardware nodes and the software artifacts deployed on them, along with communication paths.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source explicitly defines deployment diagrams as modeling physical architecture and showing hardware/software relationships.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept is a distinct, checkable idea that introduces the diagram type and its primary use, suitable for a single focused question.

candidate_concepts.label: Nodes in UML Deployment Diagrams
candidate_concepts.description: Nodes represent computational resources such as computers, sensors, printers, or servers. They can be connected by communication paths to describe network structures.
coverage_criteria: Student can define a node in UML and give examples of hardware resources that nodes represent.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Nós nos Modelos UML' defines nodes as model elements representing computational resources.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Nodes are a fundamental building block of deployment diagrams, and this concept is small enough to check with one question.

candidate_concepts.label: Node Instances in UML
candidate_concepts.description: An instance of a node represents an actual occurrence of a node, based on an existing node definition.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain that a node instance is a specific concrete occurrence of a node type.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Instâncias do Nó' describes node instances as instanciations of nodes.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a distinct but simple concept that can be checked with one question about what a node instance is.

candidate_concepts.label: Artifacts in UML
candidate_concepts.description: Artifacts are model elements that represent physical software entities like executable files, libraries, components, documents, and databases.
coverage_criteria: Student can list examples of artifacts and explain that they represent deployable software units.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Artefatos' defines artifacts as physical units of execution.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Artifacts are a core element in deployment diagrams, distinct from nodes, and can be checked with a simple listing or identification question.

candidate_concepts.label: Execution Environments in UML
candidate_concepts.description: An execution environment is a type of node that represents a specific execution platform, such as an operating system or database management system, providing context for execution.
coverage_criteria: Student can define execution environment as a node that offers a runtime platform and give examples.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Ambientes de Execução' defines execution environments as a type of node.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept is distinct from general nodes and adds to the detail of deployment diagrams, checkable with one or two questions.

candidate_concepts.label: Devices in UML Deployment Diagrams
candidate_concepts.description: A device is a type of node that represents a physical computational resource in a system, such as an application server.
coverage_criteria: Student can differentiate a device from a general node in UML deployment diagrams.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Dispositivos' defines device as a type of node representing a physical resource.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Devices are a specialized node type, and this concept isolates that specialization for focused assessment.

candidate_concepts.label: Deployment Specifications in UML
candidate_concepts.description: A deployment specification is a configuration file (e.g., XML or text) that defines how an artifact is deployed onto a node.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain that a deployment specification is a configuration artifact that guides the deployment process.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Especificações de Implementação' describes deployment specifications as configuration files.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept covers a specific type of artifact used in deployment, distinct and checkable with a single question.

candidate_concepts.label: Relationships in UML Deployment Diagrams
candidate_concepts.description: Relationships in deployment diagrams include communication paths between nodes and deployment relationships that link artifacts to nodes.
coverage_criteria: Student can identify the two primary relationship types in deployment diagrams: communication paths and deployment relationships.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Relacionamentos em Diagramas de Implementação' describes connections between model elements.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Relationships are a key structural concept, and this candidate covers the types without delving into excessive detail, suitable for a couple of questions.

candidate_concepts.label: Deployment Diagrams vs Component Diagrams
candidate_concepts.description: Deployment diagrams show where components and artifacts are used in the deployed system, while component diagrams define the composition of components and artifacts in the system.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the difference: deployment diagrams focus on physical allocation, component diagrams on logical composition.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source includes a note explicitly distinguishing deployment diagrams from component diagrams.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This distinction is a common point of confusion and is succinctly explained in the source, making it a checkable concept with one comparison question.

source_anchors.locator: Nota: Os diagramas de implementação são distintos dos diagramas de componentes.

candidate_concepts.label: Use Cases for UML Deployment Diagrams
candidate_concepts.description: Deployment diagrams are effective for modeling embedded systems, client-server systems, and distributed systems.
coverage_criteria: Student can list three types of systems for which deployment diagrams are particularly useful.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source explicitly states that deployment diagrams are effective for these three system types.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept captures the practical application context, which can be checked by listing the system types.
